text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Rising fuel costs push KLM Royal Dutch Airlines into the red in third quarter of the 1996/97 financial year. (p1)
- MPs to table questions on techno lease-back agreements made between the Rabobank, Fokker and Philips. (p1)
- Frans Swarttouw (64), former chairman of planemaker Fokker from 1978-1989 and container terminal company ECT died on Monday. (p1)
- Unions, works council and management of Rotterdam-based bulk terminal EBS reach agreement in principle on restructuring (p1).
- Delays in forging public transport links could be avoided by passing part of the costs on to new home buyers in new housing developments, public transport body Mobis proposes. (p1)
- Foods group CSM says it will limit itself to small takeover after recent series of large buy-outs. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is to sell its South African coal activities. (p4)
- Animal feeds group Nutreco asks U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs and Rabobank to investigate possible bourse flotation. (p9)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Large number of unregistered banks operating in the Netherlands conducting large cross-border cash flows. (p1)
- European Commission is to ask clarification from Dutch government about technolease construction. (p1)
- Israel's brewer Tempo offers Heineken a stake in the company of more than 44.5 percent. (p2)
- Belgium's Flemish newspaper publisher De Tijd seeks alliance with HAL Holding in proposed buy-out of Dutch financial newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dozens of major Dutch businesses discover the rights to use their own names on the Internet have been bought up by "name hijackers" at home and in Hong Kong. (p1)
- New parliamentary speaker Piet Bukman seems unable to maintain order in the House. (p1)
- Underground rail link between flower auction Aalsmeer and Schiphol Airport could be realised within seven years, if cabinet is prepared to invest one billion guilders. (p7)
- Economic affairs ministry asks independent institute STR to develop risk profile for financing biotechnology projects. (p21)
TROUW
- Dutch environment minister's proposals to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases across Europe set a target for the Netherlands of 10 pct reduction to 2010. (p1)
- New setback for chemicals concern Akzo Nobel as Germany maintains restrictions to the use of light contraceptive pill. (p6)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch rail NS and transport minister Annemarie Jorritsma reach agreement on maintaining 29 unprofitable lines. (p1)
